column1: T1: Dataset overview (ordered start/goal pairs, start != goal)
Note: The 12 synthetic graphs are 4 node layouts (12, 15, 20, 25 nodes) x 3 densities. The three densities of one layout share identical node positions; denser graphs add edges.
T2: Validation against an independent exact shortest-path calculation (Floyd-Warshall)
Note: Path valid = starts at start, ends at goal, uses only real edges, no repeated node. Costs compared exactly using fractions, not floating point.
T3: Main comparison by dataset and case type
Note: Queue pops = the existing 'nodes explored' counter in main.py: every item removed from the priority queue, including the goal and any outdated duplicate entries.
T4: How much more Greedy paid when it missed the shortest path
Note: Extra cost % = (Greedy cost - shortest cost) / shortest cost x 100, over higher-cost cases only.
T5: Synthetic non-direct cases by density
T6: Synthetic non-direct cases by layout nodes
T7: What the queue-pop count contains (non-direct cases)
Note: queue pops = expansions + skipped outdated pops + 1 goal pop. UCS skips outdated entries but still counts them. A* has no skip check, so outdated entries are expanded again (repeat expansions).
T8: Measured run time per call on one machine (indicative only)
Note: Each case: 7 timed batches x 50 calls per algorithm, algorithm order shuffled each batch (seed 2026), after warm-up runs, garbage collector off. Python 3.12.10 on Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0.
T9: Euclidean heuristic vs. rounded edge weights
Note: Weights are straight-line lengths rounded to 2 decimals; the heuristic uses the unrounded length, so it can be up to 0.005 too high.
